anchors.content: Nash notes prior machine submission and explicitly refers to a general exponential conjecture discussed with colleagues.
Defines finite key and adversary setting; distinguishes theoretical determination of the key from practical computation cost.
Direct brute force tests 2^r keys; simple cipher structure may admit much shorter shortcut computation; proposes classifying ciphers by growth of key-computation length.
States general conjecture that sufficiently complex interacting key instructions can make mean key-computation length grow exponentially with key length; draws practical-unbreakability consequence.
NSA reply says the concrete system was carefully examined but did not meet official security requirements.
NSA memorandum describes the proposed permuting ciphertext auto-key principle as ingenious but limited-security and equipment-heavy, and notes an earlier 1950 submission.
